item.title: Joe Jonas Says He Sought Therapy After His Solo Album Underperformed
item.description:
[Intro music plays, followed by the host]
Host: Welcome to Trending on Billboard. Today, we're talking about Joe Jonas and his journey to finding success and overcoming personal struggles.
[Music transitions to a softer tone]
Host: You might know Joe Jonas from his time in the Jonas Brothers, but did you know that his 2011 solo debut album, Fastlife, didn't quite live up to his expectations? It peaked at No. 15 on the Billboard 200, and its lead single "See No More" reached No. 92 on the Hot 100. For Joe, this was a tough pill to swallow.
[Short music clip of "See No More" plays]
Host: In a recent episode of the Hey Jonas! podcast, Joe opened up to his brothers, Nick and Kevin, about how the album's reception affected him. He had tied the album's success to his own self-worth, and when it didn't meet his expectations, he started experiencing panic attacks and physical pain.
[Soft music continues to play]
Host: Luckily, Joe found help through therapy, and he eventually found a new path to success with his funk-pop band DNCE. Their debut single "Cake by the Ocean" reached No. 9 on the Billboard Hot 100, and the Jonas Brothers even reunited in 2019, topping the Billboard 200 with Happiness Begins.
[Music clip of "Cake by the Ocean" plays, followed by "Sucker"]
Host: It's a great reminder that even when things don't go as planned, there's always a chance to find a new path and achieve success. Thanks for tuning in to Trending on Billboard.
[Outro music plays]
